expected_if_claim: Full three-modality Eadro beats the capacity-matched traces-only variant on HR@1, HR@5 and anomaly F1, both aggregated over TrainTicket/SocialNetwork and on most individual fault cases.
expected_if_alternative: The capacity-matched traces-only variant matches full Eadro's HR@1, HR@5 and F1 within statistical noise on the same splits and fault cases.
brief_rationale: The Table 3 claim 'Complementary telemetry improves diagnosis' accurately represents the quoted abstract interpretation. Modality-drop ablations shrink modality and capacity together, so the alternative that traces plus capacity explain the gain stays open; the matched single-modality comparison separates the accounts with splits and downstream architecture fixed.

expected_if_claim: Full multimodal DiagFusion outperforms all capacity-matched single-modal variants reusing its embedding, augmentation, GNN and classifier, on A@1/A@3/A@5 and Avg@5 (D1/D2) and on failure-type precision/recall/F1.
expected_if_alternative: One or more matched single-modal variants perform on par with full DiagFusion on the same localization and failure-type metrics.
brief_rationale: The Table 3 claim 'Multimodal fusion drives diagnosis gains' is a faithful rendering of the abstract quote. Component ablations never test single-modal variants on the identical architecture at matched capacity, so the architecture-strength alternative is compatible; the proposed matched variants isolate the multimodality contrast.

expected_if_claim: Probed under an identical fixed budget, the frozen UniDiag embedding beats the same-dimension task-agnostic baseline on the auxiliary tasks (resource prediction, cross-modality reconstruction, subgraph recovery).
expected_if_alternative: The frozen UniDiag embedding performs at or below the task-agnostic baseline of the same dimension on those auxiliary tasks under the same budget.
brief_rationale: The Table 3 claim 'Representation captures comprehensive system state' faithfully tracks the abstract quote. Classification-only evidence cannot exclude task-specific-tuning artifact. My reservation is design isolation: the 'task-agnostic baseline representation' is unspecified (random, PCA, or another pretrained embedding?), and linear-probe outcomes hinge on probe and budget choices; pre-specify a baseline family to make the comparison interpretable.

expected_if_claim: Cross-view transfer of a head trained on one modality view achieves clearly better localization HR@1/HR@3 and type F1 with TVDiag-CM than with TVDiag-without-CM or the masked-reconstruction control.
expected_if_alternative: Cross-view transfer is comparably weak across TVDiag-CM, TVDiag-without-CM and the generic-regularization control, with no significant separation.
brief_rationale: The Table 3 claim 'Features contain view-invariant fault information' faithfully reflects the abstract quote. The w/o-CM ablation cannot distinguish view-invariance from generic representation enrichment; the cross-view transfer test with a capacity-matched generic-regularization arm controls exactly that on the same datasets.

expected_if_claim: Over the widened sweep on MaxCompute, KHBN keeps high macro precision, cover rate and F1 with low coefficient of variation and a small worst-case drop, while comparison methods show larger variation.
expected_if_alternative: KHBN's coefficient of variation and worst-case drop from its best configuration grow sharply once the sweep extends well beyond the originally tested region.
brief_rationale: The Table 3 claim 'Diagnosis is robust to configuration changes' is faithful to the abstract quote (KHBN is CloudRCA's own model, so C and D are consistent). The extended sweep discriminates inherent from region-local robustness, but very small or very large parameter values can yield degenerate configurations; state explicitly how non-functional settings are excluded or reported so the comparison is not an artifact of the chosen range.

expected_if_claim: Applied to a new large-scale component with only metric-name mapping, CauseRank retains A@1/A@3/A@5 and MAR close to its Oracle results and beats comparable domain-specific baselines.
expected_if_alternative: On the new component type, CauseRank's A@1/A@3/A@5 fall well below its Oracle numbers and MAR worsens, with domain-specific baselines matching or beating it.
brief_rationale: Fidelity failure: the source quote states the framework 'can be applied to other large-scale system components' - a claim of conceptual applicability - while the Table 3 claim 'Diagnosis is generic across systems' asserts an established cross-system property that a single-Oracle evaluation cannot support. The contrast as worded misrepresents the source; reword the Table 3 claim (e.g., 'Framework designed to be generic across systems') before the Q2-Q5 judgments, which are otherwise sound: the tailoring alternative is compatible and the transfer experiment discriminates cleanly.

expected_if_claim: In blind review of AnySvc=1/PR=0 cases, expert judges find most outputs lack any correct or implied root-to-alarm causal understanding (category a dominates).
expected_if_alternative: Expert judges find most ungrounded cases already express the correct causal understanding in text, with PR failure attributable to missing edges, reversed directions or missing intermediate nodes (category b dominates).
brief_rationale: The Table 3 claim 'Outcome scoring can mask causal-process deficits' faithfully reflects the quoted 76.0%/61.5% figures. Node/Edge F1 leaves the structural-artifact alternative open. The observation targets the right contrast, but the outcome is subjective human rating; without a pre-registered rubric, inter-rater reliability statistics and an adjudication procedure the measurement may not be reproducible across rater teams.

expected_if_claim: Most sampled A->B edges pass intervention testing (high intervention-validated edge precision), and pruning to the validated subgraph keeps Precision@2 and Recall@2 close to the full learned graph, which beats a matched purely correlational graph.
expected_if_alternative: Few sampled edges survive intervention (low validated precision), and a matched purely correlational graph achieves Precision@2/Recall@2 statistically indistinguishable from the full learned graph.
brief_rationale: Fidelity is borderline: the source quote is a method-description ('we propose an approach for mining causality'), whereas the Table 3 claim 'Mined edges represent causal relations' converts it into an ontological assertion about the edges that the quoted material does not itself establish. The paper's own framing supports the stronger reading, so this is UNCERTAIN rather than NO; recommend clarifying in Table 3 that the causal status of edges is the paper's interpretation. The alternative remains compatible because retrieval accuracy never tests edge-level causality, and the intervention design discriminates the accounts.

expected_if_claim: Blind expert ratings of reasoning quality show a strong monotone association with automated Process scores across the stratified sample (high rank correlation; agreement on top- and bottom-rated outputs).
expected_if_alternative: Blind expert ratings show weak or no association with Process scores: many high-Process outputs are rated as shallow reasoning and vice versa.
brief_rationale: The Table 3 claim 'Process score captures substantive reasoning' faithfully represents the quoted reasoning-process paradigm. A template-matching agent could accumulate chain-node and checkpoint hits without genuine reasoning, so the alternative is compatible. Blinded multi-expert rating with inter-rater reliability is the appropriate external criterion and is not circular with the automated metric.

expected_if_claim: SRE participants given DeepHunt's decomposed score evidence identify the true root cause more often, decide faster and show better confidence calibration than participants given an accuracy-matched unexplained ranked list.
expected_if_alternative: The two participant groups show statistically indistinguishable root-cause identification accuracy, decision time and confidence calibration.
brief_rationale: The Table 3 claim 'Inspectable outputs help operators decide' is faithful: the added introduction quote grounds interpretability explicitly in helping operators take appropriate measures. The paper offers inspectable internals but no human-factors evidence, so the decomposability-not-utility alternative is compatible; the accuracy-matched control isolates the interpretability effect (add a familiarization phase for reading the decomposition).

expected_if_claim: Instances receiving RootCLAM-recommended actions flip from abnormal to normal at a rate significantly above both the no-intervention control and the baseline-action group, with observed effect size approximating the offline prediction.
expected_if_alternative: The observed flipping rate under real intervention barely exceeds the no-intervention control and falls well below the offline-predicted effect, indicating the actions exploit correlations rather than causal effects.
brief_rationale: The Table 3 claim 'Recommends model-based actions to revert anomalies' faithfully tracks the Section 3 quote. All flipping evidence is offline and model-conditional, so the correlation-exploitation alternative is compatible; control groups handle spontaneous recovery. Reservation: a semi-synthetic A/B whose simulator encodes the same assumed graph partially re-assumes what is tested; feasibility of genuine platform intervention should be established first.

expected_if_claim: In the full 302-incident Qwen-RAG live replay, the offline-invalid plan group restores service health within the 75-second window in only a small fraction of incidents, so the ungated live recovery rate remains close to the published validity-gated 48.3%.
expected_if_alternative: The offline-invalid group restores health in a much larger fraction of incidents than the gated statistic implied, so the ungated live recovery rate across all 302 incidents is substantially above 48.3% and the diagnosis-to-recovery gap shrinks.
brief_rationale: Corrected understanding: all 302 incidents were live-replayed and the gate applies to the recovery-rate statistic, not to execution (Section VI-E). The Table 3 claim 'Low recovery reveals a diagnosis-to-plan deficit' is consistent with the abstract's framing. Because per-group health outcomes for offline-invalid plans are undisclosed, the strict-criteria alternative remains compatible. Reporting restoration split by validity group - a re-tabulation of the same replay under identical reinjection and health windows - cleanly isolates the gating variable.
